evidence.note: The only genuine test run: cargo test -p rusternetes-common, 34 passed, marked as a milestone. After this the agent essentially never tracks test pass/fail again — it switches entirely to compile-checking.

A sustained, disciplined loop of `cargo check -p rusternetes-common` followed by `cargo check -p rusternetes-api-server --tests` after nearly every shared-crate edit — real regression-watching on a shared crate at the compilation level, maintaining a rough per-test-file build ledger.

Tracks remaining failing test files by name ('only dra_test.rs and endpointslice_handler_test.rs left'; 'all api-server tests compile except e2e_workflow_test blocked on controller-manager') — a roughly-maintained done-vs-remaining list, but purely compile status not test pass counts.
Circular debugging on the EndpointSlice Option<Vec<EndpointPort>> mismatch: repeatedly re-reads the same files confused about the error's source without cleanly recognizing it was going in circles.

Trajectory ends with 5+ crates (scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, cloud-provider, all-in-one) never touched and the full workspace suite never run — no consolidated pass/fail picture across the 100 binaries ever established.

reasoning: The agent periodically verifies state and methodically works down a list of failing crates/test files, roughly tracking remaining work — squarely anchor 5. Its consistent re-checking of the shared `common` crate plus api-server tests after edits is genuine regression-watching that reaches toward anchor 8, but the monitoring is almost entirely compilation status rather than the 1,390-test pass/fail ledger this dimension centers on (tests were actually run only once), there are no per-binary pass counts or pass/fail deltas, and one episode (steps 433-437) shows undetected circular debugging. That combination lands it at a solid 5, not higher.
